section_summary: This section contains State Department, FCC, Navy, and diplomatic correspondence from January to May 1940 regarding radio frequency interference between United States, Japanese, and regional stations. Primary issues include interference in the Far East with General Electric's shortwave broadcasting station KGEI from Japanese station JZI, Hong Kong station ZBW-3, and Thai station HS8PJ, involving disputes between the State Department and FCC over international priority of registration under the International Telecommunication Union. The records also document ongoing protests to Tokyo regarding interference caused by Japanese wireless station JND to Naval Radio Station NSS and naval communications, as well as Japanese ship interference with naval direction-finding services.

subfiles.from: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: Press Wireless reported JDK harmonic interference ceased; FCC suggests no further representations unless it recurs.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly regarding Cessation of JDK Interference with Station LJY

subfiles.about: Reporting severe interference to American shortwave station KGEI in Java from Japanese, regional, and local stations, and recommending improvements.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, American Consul General, Batavia
subfiles.summary: Consul General Dickover details reception difficulties of KGEI in Java, recommending doubled power or moving to 25 meters.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 409 from Batavia on Reception of Station KGEI in the Netherlands Indies

subfiles.about: Reviewing reception problems of KGEI in Java and explaining why the US cannot assert priority over Japanese station JZI and Hong Kong station ZBW-3.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith analyzes Bern Bureau registrations, concluding Japan and Hong Kong hold station priority over KGEI, precluding US protests.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to FCC Chairman Fly on KGEI Interference and Frequency Priority
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Informing General Electric of reception interference to KGEI in the Far East and explaining the priority standing of Japanese and Hong Kong stations.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: State informs General Electric that foreign station priority precludes protests, but efforts continue regarding Thai station HS8PJ.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to General Electric Company regarding KGEI Broadcast Interference
subfiles.to: Boyd W. Bullock, General Electric Company

subfiles.about: Acknowledging Despatch No. 409 and reporting that KGEI interference issues and remedial proposals were referred to the FCC and General Electric.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Despatch No. 409, noting its findings were sent to FCC and General Electric, but priority issues prevent formal protests.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Department of State to American Consulate General at Batavia regarding KGEI Reception

subfiles.about: Instructing the Minister to request Thai authorities to eliminate frequency deviations from station HS8PJ interfering with KGEI.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instructs Minister Neville to ask Thai authorities to eliminate frequency deviations from Bangkok station HS8PJ.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 81 from Department of State to American Legation at Bangkok regarding HS8PJ Interference
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Minister, Bangkok

subfiles.about: Reporting the Japanese Foreign Office reply maintaining Station JZI complies with radio regulations and claims priority over KGEI.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Japanese note stating JZI operates within international limits and claims priority over KGEI.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 15 from Tokyo regarding Japanese Claim of Priority for Station JZI

subfiles.about: Recording operating schedules and interference data for KGEI and JZI based on a report from the American Consul at Yokohama.
subfiles.from: Harvey B. Otterman, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Records KGEI and JZI operating hours and interference data from Yokohama Consul report.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Interference with Broadcasts of Radio Station KGEI

subfiles.about: Reporting that representations concerning radio interference by Station JND have been referred to the Japanese Ministry of Communications.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Foreign Office referred representations on JND interference to the Ministry of Communications.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 53 from Tokyo regarding Radio Interference by Japanese Station JND

subfiles.about: Transmitting a copy of Tokyo's telegram concerning interference caused by Japanese Station JND to Naval Radio Station NSS.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Tokyo Embassy telegram of January 27, 1940 regarding Japanese consideration of JND interference with NSS.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Secretary of the Navy transmitting Tokyo Telegram on Station JND
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Reasserting US priority for 9530 kc based on early notification and first use, and outlining FCC power regulations to improve KGEI reception.
subfiles.from: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: FCC asserts US priority on 9530 kc, notes 50 kw rule, and offers to consult General Electric. Includes duplicate copy.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly regarding Priority Rights and Technical Standards for Station KGEI

subfiles.about: Acknowledging FCC views and requesting to be informed of the outcome of discussions with General Electric regarding Station KGEI.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Preliminary draft acknowledging Fly's letter and requesting outcome of FCC discussions with General Electric.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from Department of State to FCC Chairman Fly regarding KGEI Discussions
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Requesting consultation before any steps are taken by FCC or General Electric and enclosing Consul General Dickover's letter.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith requests State Department consultation before FCC or General Electric take definite steps, enclosing Dickover's letter.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to FCC Chairman Fly regarding Consultations on KGEI Interference
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Transmitting Japanese Foreign Office note verbale defending JZI transmission stability and asserting priority over KGEI under international treaties.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Foreign Office note verbale defending JZI transmission stability and asserting priority over KGEI under the Madrid treaty.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4412 from Tokyo transmitting Japanese Note Verbale on Station JZI Priority

subfiles.about: Reporting Japanese authorities request more detailed technical data regarding the nature and extent of interference by Station JND.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Japanese authorities request detailed technical information on the nature and extent of JND interference.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 109 from Tokyo requesting Technical Details on Station JND Interference

subfiles.about: Instructing the Embassy to renew representations to the Japanese Foreign Office regarding ongoing JND interference with Station NSS.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Urges Embassy to renew representations to Foreign Office for prompt elimination of JND interference with NSS.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 61 from Department of State to Tokyo regarding Station JND Interference

subfiles.about: Furnishing technical parameters and Cairo Radio Regulations citations demonstrating excessive emission bandwidth and interference by Station JND.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Details technical parameters under Cairo Regulations showing JND's excessive bandwidth and strong interference at 17.8 kc.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 67 from Department of State to Tokyo providing Technical Details on Station JND

subfiles.about: Transmitting copy of telegram sent to Tokyo Embassy detailing technical interference caused by Station JND to Station NSS.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits copy of State's telegram instructing Tokyo Embassy to urge immediate cessation of JND interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Secretary of the Navy regarding Technical Data on Station JND
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Instructing urgent representations regarding Station JND communicating with German Station DFY on 17,665 kc and disrupting naval communications.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Directs urgent representations regarding JND communicating with German station DFY and disrupting naval communications at San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 107 from Department of State to Tokyo regarding Station JND Communications with German Station DFY

subfiles.about: Stating that little or no change has occurred regarding interference caused by Japanese Station JND to Naval Station NSS.
subfiles.from: Lewis Compton, Acting Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Compton reports little change in JND interference with Station NSS. Includes duplicate copy.
subfiles.title: Letter from Navy Department regarding Unchanged Station JND Interference with Station NSS

subfiles.about: Transmitting an indorsement from the Philippine Secretary of National Defense concerning signal measurements and cessation of Station JDK interference with Station KJY.
subfiles.from: Assistant Secretary, Department of the Interior
subfiles.summary: Transmits Philippine indorsement reporting signal measurements and confirming JDK interference with KJY ceased in December 1939.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of the Interior transmitting Philippine Report on Station JDK Interference

subfiles.about: Reporting continued complaints from radio listeners in Peiping regarding Japanese station JZI interfering with KGEI broadcasts.
subfiles.from: Frank P. Lockhart, American Embassy, Peiping
subfiles.summary: Lockhart reports Peiping listeners complain of JZI interference preventing reception of KGEI broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 56 from Peiping regarding Station JZI Interference with KGEI Broadcasts

subfiles.about: Informing that representations to Japan regarding KGEI were unsuccessful and the matter is under study with the FCC and General Electric.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Hull advises representations to Japan failed, but State, FCC, and General Electric are studying practicable solutions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 35 from Department of State to Peiping regarding KGEI Interference

subfiles.about: Discussing policy disagreements with the FCC over Bern Bureau priority rules and handling KGEI power increases.
subfiles.from: Harvey B. Otterman, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Otterman reviews disagreement with FCC over Bern Bureau priority and anticipates Japanese protests if KGEI power increases.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Otterman to Burke regarding Priority Conflict with FCC over Station KGEI
subfiles.to: Thomas Burke, Chief, Division of International Communications

subfiles.about: Reporting cooperation with General Electric on temporary measures for KGEI, including a 50 kw power increase and frequency time-sharing.
subfiles.from: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: Fly outlines temporary relief for KGEI via 50 kw power increase and frequency time-sharing.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly regarding Temporary Solutions for Station KGEI Reception

subfiles.about: Transmitting confidential background information on FCC and General Electric plans for KGEI power increase and frequency time-sharing.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Confidentially informs Tokyo that KGEI power will increase to 50 kw and time-sharing is under consideration.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 81 from Department of State to Tokyo regarding Technical Adjustments for Station KGEI

subfiles.about: Reporting that representations concerning Japanese interference with US naval direction finding service were referred to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports interim Foreign Office reply stating direction-finding interference was referred to competent authorities.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 152 from Tokyo regarding Direction Finding Interference Representations

subfiles.about: Reporting that a diplomatic note protesting JND interference was prepared and will be delivered after a Japanese holiday.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports protest note prepared and awaiting delivery after a Japanese holiday.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 229 from Tokyo regarding Delivery of Representations on Station JND

subfiles.about: Reporting repeated representations to the Japanese Foreign Office regarding Station JND interference with naval communications.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew reports pressing Foreign Office three times regarding JND interference, with early action promised.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 236 from Tokyo regarding Pressing Foreign Office on Station JND Interference

subfiles.about: Transmitting Japanese Foreign Office note verbale stating US representations on JND interference were referred to relevant authorities.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Foreign Office note verbale acknowledging representations on JND interference with Station NSS.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4566 from Tokyo transmitting Foreign Office Note on Station JND Interference

subfiles.about: Transmitting a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 4566 concerning Japanese Station JND interference with Naval Radio Station NSS.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 4566 and Foreign Office note regarding JND interference to the Navy Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Secretary of the Navy transmitting Despatch on Station JND
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Reporting Japanese Foreign Office assurances that instructions were sent to prevent ship radio interference with US naval direction finding.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Foreign Office issued instructions and will take special measures on two ships to prevent direction-finding interference.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 243 from Tokyo regarding Measures on Direction Finding Interference by Japanese Ships

subfiles.about: Transmitting a copy of Tokyo Telegram No. 243 concerning Japanese ship interference with naval direction finding on 375 kilocycles.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Tokyo telegram reporting Japanese measures to prevent vessel interference with naval direction finding.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Secretary of the Navy transmitting Tokyo Telegram on Direction Finding
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Clarifying operating frequencies and schedules of Thai stations and reporting that station HS8PJ discontinued operating on 9510 kc.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, American Minister, Bangkok
subfiles.summary: Neville details Thai broadcast schedules, confirming station HS8PJ discontinued operating on 9510 kc on December 1, 1939.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 644 from Bangkok on Alleged Radio Interference by Thai Stations

subfiles.about: Informing that Thai station HS8PJ changed call letters to HSP6, moved to 7968 kc, and ceased operating on 9510 kc in December 1939.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Advises FCC that Thai station HS8PJ was renamed HSP6, moved to 7968 kc, and left 9510 kc.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to FCC Chairman Fly regarding Thai Radio Station Changes
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: Informing General Electric that Thai station HS8PJ changed to HSP6 and discontinued broadcasting on 9510 kc.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs General Electric that Thai station HS8PJ became HSP6, moved to 7968 kc, and left 9510 kc.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to General Electric Company regarding Thai Station Changes

subfiles.about: Informing Consul General Dickover of frequency changes by Thai station HS8PJ and inquiring if KGEI interference has ceased.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs Batavia of Thai frequency changes and inquires if KGEI interference has ceased in Java.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Department of State to American Consulate General at Batavia regarding Thai Station Changes
subfiles.to: Erle R. Dickover, American Consul General, Batavia

subfiles.about: Reporting clear reception of KGEI and requesting more American domestic and political news rather than European rebroadcasts.
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, American Ambassador, Chungking
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Johnson reports clear KGEI reception and suggests adding American domestic and political campaign news.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 188 from Chungking regarding Station KGEI Reception and Program Content

subfiles.about: Welcoming clear reception of KGEI and noting Ambassador Johnson's comments on program content were forwarded to General Electric.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Gratified by clear KGEI reception and notes programming suggestions were forwarded to General Electric.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 81 from Department of State to Chungking regarding Station KGEI Program Content

subfiles.about: Transmitting Ambassador Johnson's suggestion to include more US domestic and political campaign news in KGEI broadcasts to the Far East.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Ambassador Johnson's suggestion that KGEI carry more domestic political and convention news.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to General Electric Company regarding Station KGEI Program Content

subfiles.about: Advising that General Electric promised careful consideration of the Ambassador's recommendations for KGEI news broadcasts.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs Ambassador Johnson that General Electric will carefully consider his programming suggestions for KGEI.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Department of State to American Embassy at Chungking regarding KGEI Programming
subfiles.to: Nelson T. Johnson, American Ambassador, Chungking

subfiles.about: Acknowledging notification regarding call letter and frequency changes of Thai radio station HSP6.
subfiles.from: B. J. Rowan, Assistant to Manager of Broadcasting, General Electric Company
subfiles.summary: General Electric acknowledges notice of frequency and call letter changes for Thai station HSP6.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Electric Company regarding Thai Radio Station Changes
subfiles.to: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Assuring that careful consideration will be given to Ambassador Johnson's comments concerning KGEI news programming.
subfiles.from: B. J. Rowan, Assistant to Manager of Broadcasting, General Electric Company
subfiles.summary: General Electric assures careful consideration will be given to Ambassador Johnson's suggestions regarding KGEI programming.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Electric Company regarding KGEI News Broadcast Content
subfiles.to: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Acknowledging notification that Thai station HSP6 changed operating frequency from 9510 kc to 7968 kc.
subfiles.from: James Lawrence Fly, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.summary: Chairman Fly acknowledges report that Thai station HSP6 moved from 9510 kc to 7968 kc.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly regarding Thai Radio Station Frequency Changes

subfiles.about: Transmitting Embassy Note No. 1512 protesting JND communications with German station DFY and Foreign Office reply Note No. 76.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Embassy Note No. 1512 protesting JND communications with DFY and Foreign Office reply Note No. 76.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4643 from Tokyo transmitting Representations and Reply on Station JND Interference

subfiles.about: Transmitting a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 4643 and enclosures concerning Japanese Station JND interference with naval communications.
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 4643 regarding JND interference with naval communications to Secretary Edison.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Secretary of the Navy transmitting Despatch on Station JND
subfiles.to: Charles Edison, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Transmitting the Japanese Foreign Office reply to representations regarding Japanese vessel interference with US naval direction finding.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4607 from Tokyo regarding Foreign Office Reply on Naval Direction Finding Interference
